subject: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff & congestion mitigation
messages:
From: Ops Lead <ops-lead@embercloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@embercloud.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff for EmberCloud

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for agreeing to help us size a private GPU pool for our inference workloads. Our goal is to run a customer-facing recommendation API in our VPC and hit a steady-state 25k tokens/sec (aggregate across model variants) with p95 latency under 220ms for single-turn generation at 768 tokens. We have a hard network egress cap of 15Gbps from our rack and want to avoid bursting policies that cause opaque throttling.

Key constraints:
- Production timeline: staggered rollout starting mid-November; procurement needs sizing numbers by Sep 15.
- Regulatory: logs must stay in our VPC for 90 days.
- Workload: mixed short chat (avg 64 tokens) and occasional long batching jobs for analytics.

Can you provide an initial capacity plan, recommended GPU types, expected headroom for spiky traffic, and networking mitigations (eg. QoS, multi-subnet routing)? Attaching our current topology export.

Regards,
Sam Ortiz
Head of Ops, EmberCloud
Attachment: embercloud-svc-constraints.pdf (pdf, 85KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Lead <ops-lead@embercloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff for EmberCloud

Sam —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Quick notes and a few clarifying questions before we put numbers behind procurement:

1) Throughput/Latency targets: we can commit to aggregate throughput targets in Dedicated/Private, but p95 latency depends heavily on batching and KV prefix reuse. Is the 25k tokens/sec target sustained 24/7 or peak-minute?
2) Network: is the 15Gbps cap bi-directional or egress-only? Also any per-subnet MTU limits?
3) Models: do you plan to serve multiple model sizes (e.g., 13B quantized + 70B quantized) or a single family? That affects KV memory and GPU memory footprint.

I'll loop in Marissa for the internal capacity math and Aditya for routing/fallback policy recommendations. We'll produce: (a) a conservative GPU-count baseline, (b) headroom plan (spike absorb + degraded-mode), (c) suggested QoS & multiplexing topology, and (d) a short test-plan for acceptance. Expect the draft by Tue EOD PST.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ops Lead <ops-lead@embercloud.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff for EmberCloud

Kimberly / Sam —

Draft capacity summary (conservative baseline + suggested resiliency):

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Target sustained throughput: 25,000 tokens/sec aggregate (24/7)
- Traffic mix: 70% short-chat (~64 tokens), 30% long-gen (~768 tokens)
- Model mix: primary 13B quantized (Q4_0) for short-chat, optional 70B quantized for long-gen during non-peak windows
- Preferred GPU: A100 40GB (q4/quantization path optimized). We can propose 80GB A100 if you expect large KV + 70B baseline.

Baseline sizing:
- Single A100 40GB throughput (conservative estimate with Redwood runtime): ~1,400 tokens/sec for mixed requests under steady batching.
- For 25k tokens/sec baseline: 25,000 / 1,400 = ~18 GPUs. Recommend starting with 20 GPUs to allow maintenance and small node failures.

Headroom & scaling policy:
- Target safety margin: +25% headroom => run 25 GPUs (handles sustained + typical spikes).
- Burst buffer: allow 20% temporary burst above headroom via warm pool of pre-warmed containers on additional nodes (cold-start penalty avoided).
- Degraded mode: fallback to smaller model variants or reduced max_tokens for best-effort during network congestion. Redwood runtime supports automatic variant fallback by route.

Networking notes:
- With 25 GPUs, expected network egress (model outputs only, conservative): assume avg token payload 2 bytes/token => 50KB/s per 1k tokens => ~1.25MB/s per 25k tokens? (This is optimistic; include protocol/chunking overhead). More realistic: account for TLS overhead and HTTP framing => plan for 1.5-2x => plan 30-40Mbps sustained for generated payloads.
- KV + model weights transfer between nodes: negligible once loaded; but cache warmups at rollout can spike cross-host traffic. Pre-pull model shards during low-traffic windows via staged rollout.
- Your 15Gbps rack egress cap is ample for output payloads; primary concern is control-plane and model sync spikes. Recommend dedicating a subnet for inference egress with QoS to cap non-inference traffic during peaks.

Acceptance test plan (short):
1) Synthetic traffic generator that reproduces 70/30 split at increasing levels: 10k, 20k, 25k, 30k tokens/sec.
2) Measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and token/sec per GPU, monitor KV hit-rate, and cold-start rate.
3) Network soak: verify egress cap handling at 15Gbps while maintaining p95 < 220ms with degraded-mode enabled.

Deliverables we will attach: sizing table (GPU counts, memory, expected token/sec/GPU), a short runbook for warm-pool orchestration, and a network QoS checklist.

Attaching the initial runbook and a quick topology sketch for your ops team.

Attachments: private-pool-sizing-runbook.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB); network-topology-diagram.png (png, 240KB)

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Ops Lead <ops-lead@embercloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@embercloud.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff for EmberCloud

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A couple clarifications and constraints from my infra team:

- 25k tokens/sec is our target peak-minute goal; sustained during business hours is expected to be ~18k tokens/sec. Peak + concurrent analytics batch windows drive the worst-case.
- 15Gbps is egress-only from our rack. Internal cross-host fabric is a separate 100Gbps spine.
- We have strict burst limits on cross-AZ traffic; can't rely on cross-AZ model pulls to absorb spikes.

Questions:
1) If we shift to mixed GPU types (some 80GB + some 40GB) to handle 70B occasionally, how would that change the baseline count?
2) Can you provide an explicit degraded-mode config example that reduces token budget per request and fallback decision tree so our engineers can implement it?

Procurement needs the baseline and the 25% headroom case in a simple table for the vendor quote by Sep 10. Also looping in a security reviewer next — they will ask for a short explanation of how logs remain in our VPC and how KMS keys are managed during Private deployment.

—Sam
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Lead <ops-lead@embercloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool capacity kickoff for EmberCloud

Sam —

Follow-ups / action items from Redwood side:

1) Sizing table (attached): baseline (20x A100-40GB), 25% headroom (25x A100-40GB). If EmberCloud mixes in 2x A100-80GB nodes for the 70B profile, we can reduce baseline by ~2 GPUs (so baseline 18x40GB + 2x80GB equivalent to ~20 effective nodes) — I'll add that explicit matrix into the spreadsheet.

2) Degraded-mode config: we'll provide a route-level policy example for your Envoy that does: prefer model-13B -> if latency breach or network-congestion signal then 1) reduce max_tokens by 35%, 2) switch to quantized-13B-small, 3) if still failing, return 503 with standard retry-after and switch to cached-template response. I'll paste a compact YAML snippet into the runbook.

3) KMS/logs: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) and S3-compatible logging that stays inside your VPC; we'll document the exact key rotation expectations for your security reviewer.

4) Test plan and schedule: we'll deliver the acceptance artifact and the synthetic load harness by Fri 2026-09-03. Let's set a 45-minute sync on Sep 6 to review the procurement-ready table and security notes. Proposed: Mon Sep 6 10:00 AM PT.

Next steps for us (Kim/Marissa/Aditya): finalize the spreadsheet with the mixed-GPU math, add the degraded-mode YAML, and a short checklist for QoS + pre-pull windows. I'll upload the final artifacts to the Drive link and send to procurement.

Thanks — appreciate the clear constraints.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
